text: By 2050, many experts believe we will see the arrival of artificial general intelligence, or AGI. Unlike the narrow AI we use today for specific tasks like language translation or facial recognition, AGI would be able to learn and reason across any field, much like a human. The potential benefits are enormous: AGI could help us cure diseases, solve climate change, or even manage global supply chains efficiently. However, risks are equally real, from widespread job displacement to issues of control and safety. While some predict AGI within a decade, others think it may take much longer. The future, therefore, depends not just on technological progress, but on how wisely we prepare for it.
